annotation.title_clean: Trustworthiness and Well-Being: The Ethical, Legal, and Social Challenge of Robotic Assistance
annotation.title_en: Trustworthiness and Well-Being: The Ethical, Legal, and Social Challenge of Robotic Assistance
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Beetz, M.; Engel, U.; Hoyer, N.; Kähler, L.; Langer, H.; Schultheis, H.; et al.
annotation.venue: Robots in Care and Everyday Life, SpringerBriefs in Sociology
annotation.summary_en: Opening chapter of a SpringerBrief presenting a conceptual framework for trust and well-being in robotic assistance in care and daily life. Using the Bremen AI Delphi population survey, it links trust and acceptance to openness to innovation and anticipated well-being, and finds respondents want robots kept out of care, private life and education.
key_provisions_or_claims: Social acceptance is a precondition for diffusion of robotic assistance.
Trust in robots rests on perceived capability, safeness and ethical adequacy.
Openness to innovation shapes acceptance via anticipated well-being in human-robot interaction.
Survey respondents prefer robots in industry, space and deep-sea, but not in care, private life or education.
Cites the EU's trustworthy-AI guidelines and White Paper 'ecosystem of trust'.
